blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Preference-aligned LLMs can exhibit mode collapse, concentrating their output distributions around a narrow set of high-reward responses. This limits creative generation, which requires quality, novelty, and diversity. Existing test-time methods often emphasize diversity, giving less attention to whether individual responses are both high-quality and novel. This distinction matters in practical use, where users may seek a single compelling, original response. We formalize creative generation as a multi-objective distributional optimization problem and introduce SEPO, a training-free framework for System Prompt Ensemble Optimization. The framework combines prompt evolution with greedy max-min selection to identify behaviorally distinct system prompts under a quality constraint, then uniformly samples one prompt per response at inference time. Across four creative generation tasks with increasing quality requirements and three open-weight models, SEPO ranks first in 8 of 12 settings on the harmonic mean of quality, diversity, and novelty, while no baseline leads in more than two. On average, it raises LLM-judged diversity from 1.92 to 3.43 and novelty from 1.00 to 3.34 over base sampling (1-5 scale), with quality decreasing from 3.72 to 3.30. We further show that expanding the optimized ensemble increases separation among prompt-conditioned response distributions. These results support system prompt ensemble optimization as a promising approach to improving LLM creativity at inference time.

blocks.en:

However, preference-aligned models can exhibit mode collapse , concentrating
their outputs around a narrow range of response

in wording while sharing the same underlying ideas, narrative structures,
or perspectives. This homogeneity limits creative applications, where
exploring distinct possibilities is itself
valuable ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) .

Although training-based approaches
have begun incorporating multiple creativity
signals ( Ismayilzada et al., 2025 ) , balancing these dimensions
without updating model parameters remains challenging. As compared in Figure 1 , existing
test-time approaches modify token sampling, elicit multiple candidates
in one generation, or condition subsequent responses on previous
outputs ( Minh et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) .
These interventions can increase variation, but their benefits must
also be assessed in terms of quality and novelty. System prompts offer
another mechanism, eliciting different approaches, styles, and
perspectives from a fixed model. Whereas conventional ensembling
aggregates generations to identify a reliable or consistent
answer ( Jiang et al., 2020 ; Wang et al., 2023 ) , creative generation can
benefit from retaining distinct prompt-conditioned behaviors as
components of a response distribution. However, differently worded prompts
may induce similar responses. The central challenge is therefore to
identify prompts that elicit complementary behaviors while maintaining
acceptable quality.

blocks.en:
We introduce System Prompt Ensemble Optimization (SEPO) , a
test-time framework that models generation as a uniform mixture of
system-prompt-conditioned response distributions
(Section 3 ). To expand behavioral
coverage while preserving quality, SEPO combines LLM-based prompt
evolution with greedy max–min selection: each selected prompt must
satisfy an estimated quality threshold and maximize its minimum
behavioral dissimilarity to the reference set. A token-level
Jensen–Shannon divergence surrogate captures differences in induced
behavior, while clustering candidate prompts maintains diverse search
directions. To encourage both ensemble complementarity and departure
from baseline behavior, the reference set includes selected prompts
and the default instruction; the latter is excluded from the final
mixture. At inference time, SEPO uniformly samples one optimized system
prompt per response and queries the fixed model.

blocks.en:
We evaluate SEPO against five test-time baselines on four datasets
spanning divergent thinking, creative writing, and mathematical
reasoning, using three open-weight instruction-tuned models.
All lexical, embedding-based, and LLM-judged evaluations show strong joint
performance across quality, diversity, and novelty. Across all 12
model–dataset combinations, SEPO ranks first in 8 on the harmonic mean of the three
LLM-judged scores, while no baseline leads in more than two. On average, it
raises diversity from 1.92 to 3.43 and novelty from 1.00 to 3.34 over base
sampling (1–5 scale), with quality decreasing from 3.72 to 3.30. Further analysis shows that expanding
the optimized ensemble increases response diversity on Artificial
Hivemind and Creative Math. Ablations confirm the value of selecting
prompts by induced behavior rather than prompt similarity, with
clustering supporting exploration and quality gating preserving quality.
These findings support behavioral ensemble optimization as a promising
approach to balancing quality, diversity, and novelty.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Creativity is a compound capacity encompassing quality, novelty, and diversity. Existing creativity benchmarks provide holistic frameworks for evaluating LLM creativity across diverse scenarios ( Hou et al., 2026 ; Ruan et al., 2026 ) , consistently revealing that performance on one creative dimension or domain rarely generalizes to others. To improve LLM creativity across all three dimensions, training-based methods have proposed weighted combinations of multi-dimensional creativity signals ( Ismayilzada et al., 2025 ) . However, training is computationally expensive and restricted to open-weight models.
Test-time methods offer a cost-efficient alternative that requires no weight
updates. Decoding-based methods such as AdapT ( Zhu et al., 2024 ) , min- p p sampling ( Minh et al., 2025 ) , and REAL sampling ( Chang et al., 2025 ) adaptively adjust sampling hyperparameters to balance factuality and diversity,
yet none explicitly targets novelty. Prompt-based methods such as denial
prompting ( Lu et al., 2025b ) , Multi-Novelty ( Lagzian et al., 2025 ) ,
GuidedSampling ( Handa et al., 2026 ) , and verbalized
sampling ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) steer generation
through instruction or context augmentation, achieving partial gains in novelty
or diversity but leaving quality underoptimized. As shown in
Table 1 , no existing test-time method
jointly optimizes all three creativity objectives: quality
( 𝒥 Qual \mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{Qual}} ), diversity ( 𝒥 Div \mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{Div}} ), and
novelty ( 𝒥 Nov \mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{Nov}} ). We address this gap with
the first test-time framework that optimizes all three under
a unified distributional objective.

blocks.en: Prompt ensembles improve answer reliability by aggregating outputs across multiple prompt variants, thereby reducing variance stemming from the sensitivity of LLMs to superficial phrasing differences ( Jiang et al., 2020 ) . Self-Consistency ( Wang et al., 2023 ) introduced a foundational form of output-level ensembling, wherein multiple reasoning chains are sampled from a single prompt and the most frequent answer is selected via majority vote, yielding significant gains on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks. Subsequent work extends this paradigm by diversifying the prompt pool itself: DIVERSE ( Li et al., 2023 ) constructs varied few-shot exemplar sets to elicit a broader distribution of reasoning paths, while Universal Self-Consistency ( Chen et al., 2024 ) generalizes majority voting to open-ended generation by prompting the model to self-select the most consistent answer among candidates. Beyond reasoning tasks, prompt paraphrasing and meta-prompting ( Suzgun & Kalai, 2024 ) demonstrate that ensembling across semantically equivalent but syntactically distinct prompts can yield calibration benefits analogous to classical model ensembles. However, these approaches are fundamentally oriented toward answer convergence, selecting the most reliable or consistent response, rather than toward fostering diverse and novel outputs, which is the goal our work addresses.
blocks.zh: 即时综艺通过汇总多个即时变体的产出来提高答案的可靠性,从而减少由于LLMs对表面用词差异的敏感性而产生的差异(Jiang等,2020年)。 自相容性(Wang等,2023年)引入了产出级综艺的基础形式,即从单一的瞬间取出多条推理链的样本,并用多数票选择最常的答案,在算术和常识推理基准上取得了显著收益. 随后的工作扩展了这一范式,使迅速集合本身多样化: DIVERSE(Li等,2023年)构建了多镜头的样板集,以引出推理路径的更广泛分布;而"普世自相通"(Chen等,2024年)则通过促使模型在候选人中自行选择最一致的答案,将多数投票普遍化为无限制一代. 除了推理任务外,迅速抛写和元推想(Suzgun & Kalai, 2024年)表明,跨等效的综艺活动,但从策略上看与古典模式综艺活动相似的分解效益。 然而,这些方法从根本上着眼于答案趋同,选择最可靠或一致的对策,而不是促进多样化和新的产出,这是我们工作所要处理的目标。

blocks.en: Automatic prompt optimization reduces the need for manual prompt design. AutoPrompt ( Shin et al., 2020 ) , Prompt Tuning ( Lester et al., 2021 ) , and Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE) ( Zhou et al., 2023 ) optimize discrete prompts or continuous embeddings, while DSPy 1 1 1 https://dspy.ai/ supports programmatic pipeline optimization. More recent methods use output comparisons ( Xiang et al., 2025 ) or numerical rewards and textual feedback ( Ren et al., 2026 ) to guide optimization. These approaches primarily target task performance, while Multi-expert Prompting ( Long et al., 2024 ) aggregates or selects responses from multiple perspectives to improve answer quality. Closer to our work, Rainbow Teaming ( Samvelyan et al., 2024 ) searches for diverse, effective adversarial prompts, and Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback ( Bradley et al., 2024 ) evolves populations of high-quality, diverse texts. SEPO instead optimizes a reusable system prompt ensemble based on the behavioral dissimilarity of induced response distributions under a quality constraint. It encourages separation from both selected prompts and a default instruction, promoting complementary behaviors and departure from baseline generation. Uniformly sampling one optimized prompt per response yields a mixture designed to support quality, diversity, and novelty.

blocks.en: Evaluating model creativity requires considering both individual responses and the distribution over them: a creative model should produce useful, varied, and unexpected responses. We therefore adopt a distributional view, defining optimization objectives over how probability mass is allocated across the entire response space, while retaining the quality and novelty of individual samples as objectives.

blocks.en: 4 System Prompt Ensemble Optimization for Creative Generation

blocks.en:
Aligned LLMs concentrate probability mass on a narrow set of typical
responses, so repeated sampling often yields near-duplicate
outputs ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) . Since
different system prompts steer a model toward different generation
behaviors, we introduce SEPO (System Prompt Ensemble Optimization),
which optimizes an ensemble of system prompts without updating model
parameters. Guided by the creativity metrics in
Section 3 , SEPO combines
prompt evolution with greedy max–min selection to identify
behaviorally distinct prompts that satisfy a quality threshold. At
inference time, it samples one optimized system prompt per
response. Figure 1 compares this
procedure with the baselines.

blocks.en: For each dataset, we use five random training prompts and run 10 rounds (4 evolution steps per round, 4 seeds per step, 4 proposals per seed) with gpt-oss-20b as proposer and judge; JS Divergence uses two rollouts per system prompt–task prompt pair, capped at 32 tokens (Appendix C ). We evaluate the three dimensions from Section 3 : quality via mean LLM-judge Likert scores (1–5) ( Gu et al., 2025 ) , and diversity (within-prompt variation) and novelty (departure from a baseline pool) via LLM-judge, embedding-, and n n -gram-based metrics (Appendix J ). Because responses may appear diverse or original while remaining low-quality or failing to satisfy the task requirements, we evaluate methods jointly through their quality–diversity and quality–novelty trade-offs. We use the harmonic mean to summarize performance across dimensions, following Padmakumar et al. (2026) , who define novelty as the harmonic mean of quality and originality to penalize originality gained at the expense of quality.

blocks.en: 6.1 Improving LLM Creativity through System Prompt Ensembles with SEPO
blocks.zh: 6.1 改进LLM 通过 SEPO 的系统提示集

blocks.en: Figure 3 plots quality against embedding-based diversity and novelty; methods closer to the upper-right corner, on greener contours, achieve a better balance. On Qwen3-1.7B, SEPO substantially improves diversity and novelty over base and min- p p sampling while largely preserving quality, staying above the required minimum (dashed line) on all four datasets at every temperature. It thus elicits varied, novel responses without the pronounced quality degradation of verbalized sampling. The n n -gram-based results (Figures 14 and 15 ) also show generally higher lexical diversity and novelty than base and min- p p sampling, so the optimized ensembles increase both semantic and lexical variation while retaining task quality.
blocks.zh: 图3 与嵌入式多样性和新颖性相比的质量;更接近于更绿色轮廓上右上角的方法实现更好的平衡。 在Qwen3-1.7B上,SEPO大大改进了基础和min-p采样上的多样性和新颖性,同时在很大程度上保持了质量,在每个温度下,在所有四个数据集上都保持在所需的最低值(干线)以上. 因此,它引起了各种各样的新颖反应,而没有使口头抽样的质量明显地退化。 n-gram基结果(图14和图15)也显示一般比碱基和min-p sample更高的语法多样性和新颖性,因此最优化的合唱团在保留任务质量的同时会增加语义和语法上的差异.

blocks.en: Base and min- p p sampling retain high quality but yield limited embedding-based diversity and novelty, even at higher temperatures; their lexical diversity also declines as temperature decreases. Verbalized sampling increases variation at a severe quality cost, falling below the required minimum on three of the four datasets, while Multi-Turn sampling generally offers a less favorable balance than SEPO.

blocks.en: Embedding- and n n -gram-based metrics are scalable proxies for semantic and lexical diversity/novelty, but may miss subtler differences in creative responses. We therefore also evaluate quality, diversity, and novelty using an LLM judge. For Qwen3-1.7B, SEPO has the highest harmonic mean of the three scores, 0.85, against 0.72 for SEP, the strongest baseline, and 0.42 for base sampling (Table 2 (a)). SEPO matches SEP on Novelty Bench and outperforms every baseline on the other three datasets (Figure 5 ).

blocks.en: 6.2 Generalizing across Model Families and Model Sizes
blocks.zh: 6.2 泛指模范家庭和模范规模

blocks.en: We repeat the comparison across all 12 model–dataset scenarios. A creative method should do well on quality, diversity, and novelty at once , so we compare methods by the harmonic mean of the three judge scores, which drops sharply if any one is low (Figure 5 ). SEPO ranks first in 8 of the 12 scenarios, and no baseline in more than two. Compared with base sampling, SEPO raises average diversity from 1.92 to 3.43 and novelty from 1.00 to 3.34, while quality drops from 3.72 to 3.30, still above 3, the rubric’s level for competent, on-task responses (Table 2 (a)). Verbalized sampling has the highest novelty (3.67), but its quality falls to 2.35, below this level. We also ask how often a method comes close to the best on all three dimensions. We call this joint coverage : the share of scenarios in which every score is within a given tolerance of the best score (Table 2 (b)). SEPO stays within 30% of the best in 11 of the 12 scenarios, against 7 for the strongest baseline, and no baseline surpasses it at any tolerance tested (Table 9 ).
blocks.zh: 我们重复所有12个模型-数据集情景的比较。 一个创造性的方法应该同时在质量、多样性和新颖性上做得很好,所以我们用三位法官的口音平均值来比较方法,如果任何一个评分都很低,则会急剧下降(图5)。 SEPO在12个情景中的8个中排名第一,在2个以上没有基线. 与基准采样相比,SEPO将平均多样性从1.92提高到3.43,新颖性从1.00提高到3.34,而质量则从3.72下降到3.30,仍然高于3,即胜任的、任务答复(表2(a))。 虚化的采样具有最高的新颖性(3.67),但其质量下降到2.35,低于这一水平. 我们还问,在所有三个方面,一种方法如何经常接近最佳。 我们称之为联合报道:每个得分都在最佳得分的一定容忍度范围内的情景(表2(b))。 在12个假设中,有11个假设中,SEPO保持在最佳水平的30%以内,而最强基线为7个,在任何测试的耐受度中,任何基线都不超过这一水平(表9)。

blocks.en: We apply the ten prompts searched on Qwen3-1.7B to Qwen3-30B-A3B (mixture-of-experts) and Qwen3-32B (dense). The gains persist on both larger models, so prompts found by searching on a small model can be reused on larger ones. Appendix O provides all metrics, comparisons with prompts searched on the target, and transfer across model families.

blocks.en: Having established that SEPO’s gains are consistent, we examine why the optimized ensemble helps (Figure 6 ). (a) The search keeps finding distinct prompts. SEPO admits one system prompt per round, scoring each candidate by its smallest JS divergence to the prompts already selected (Appendix D ). This score stays well above zero in all ten rounds, so every admitted prompt induces a response distribution distinct from all earlier ones. (b) Distinct prompts add diversity. With the number of responses fixed at 20, embedding diversity on Creative Math rises from 0.071 with one prompt to 0.101 with ten, always above base sampling; the gain thus comes from mixing prompts, not from drawing more samples. (c) The mixture components are separable. For an example Artificial Hivemind prompt, responses from the ten optimized prompts occupy largely distinct regions of the embedding space, whereas base responses form one compact cluster (all prompts in Appendix F ). Together, these results support the mixture interpretation of SEPO: combining behaviorally distinct prompt-conditioned distributions broadens the model’s effective response space.
blocks.zh: 在确定SEPO的得益一致之后,我们审视了优化后的组合为何有帮助(图6)。 (a) 搜索不断发现明显的提示。 SEPO每轮录取一个系统,将每个候选人根据其最小的JS差异来评分到已经选定的提示(附录D)。 这个分数在所有十轮中都保持了远远高于零,因此每一次被承认的迅速会诱发一个与所有前作不同的响应分布. (b) 有区别的提示增加了多样性。 随着答复数量固定在20个,将多样性嵌入到 " 创造数学 " 上,从0.071起,一个快取出一个快取出10个快取出0.101起,始终高于基准采出;因此,收益来自混合的快取,而不是取出更多的样本。 (c) 混合物成分可分离。 例如,人工蜂窝即时反应,来自10个最优化的蜂窝即时反应占据了嵌入空间的大致不同的区域,而基础反应则形成一个紧凑的集群(附录F的所有提示)。 这些结果共同支持了SEPO的混合解释:结合行为区别的即时分布,拓宽了模型的有效反应空间.

blocks.en: 6.4 Isolating What Drives SEPO ’s Gains
blocks.zh: 6.4 孤立什么驱动SEPO的收获

blocks.en: Ablation results confirm that each component of SEPO contributes to its overall performance. Replacing clustering with global JS-divergence Top-4 selection moderately reduces diversity and novelty, while replacing response-level JS divergence with instruction cosine similarity causes substantially larger drops across all four creativity metrics, highlighting the importance of behavior-space optimization. Finally, removing either the instruction-level or response-level quality gate decreases quality significantly, showing that both gates are necessary to preserve response quality.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusions

blocks.en:
Creativity is not a one-dimensional metric; it involves multiple dimensions that
must be considered together. We introduce a formal definition of LLM creativity
as a multi-objective distributional optimization problem, with quality,
diversity, and novelty defined as objectives over a model’s response
distribution. These dimensions are not interchangeable: a model can be high
quality without being diverse, diverse without being novel, or novel without
being useful. Improving creativity therefore requires optimizing all three
jointly, rather than trading one for another.

Guided by this distributional view, we
introduce SEPO, a test-time framework that optimizes system prompt ensembles by
combining prompt evolution with behavioral max–min selection under a quality
constraint. Experiments across four datasets and three open-weight models
demonstrate strong joint performance relative to five test-time baselines, and
further analyses highlight the importance of behavioral selection and quality
gating. These results support system prompt ensemble optimization as a practical
approach to eliciting diverse and novel responses from fixed models.

blocks.en:
Two directions merit further study. First, our approach operates at test time
and keeps model parameters fixed; future work could examine whether combining it
with post-training further broadens the range of responses while maintaining
quality. Second, our evaluation relies primarily on automatic metrics. As LLMs
are increasingly used to generate creative content, human studies could clarify
how readers judge novelty and diversity, and how closely automatic metrics
reflect those judgments.

blocks.en: In this section, we analyze the three types of diversity and novelty metrics we used to evaluate the performance of all methods on creative generation. Embedding-based metrics ( Jiang et al., 2026 ) , N-gram-based metrics ( Cao et al., 2026 ) , and LLM-as-a-Judge metrics ( Hou et al., 2026 ) are all widely used to evaluate creative generation tasks. However, there has been little discussion of the agreement or reliability across these three types of metrics, which calls into question the use of automatic metrics such as embedding-based and N-gram-based metrics. Here, we provide a preliminary analysis to better understand how these metrics relate to one another and to ground our use of automatic metrics. Specifically, we investigate three questions about diversity and novelty metrics for creative generation: (1) To what extent do embedding-based, N-gram-based, and LLM-as-a-Judge metrics agree with one another? (2) How reliable is each family of metrics? (3) Are embedding-based metrics robust to the choice of embedding model?
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们分析了我们用来评价所有方法在创造性生成方面的表现的三种多样性和新颖性衡量标准。 基于嵌入的度量衡(Jiang等,2026年),以N克为基准的度量衡(Cao等,2026年),以及LLM-as-a-judge 度量衡(Hou等,2026年)都被广泛用于评价创造性生成任务. 然而,对于这三类衡量标准之间的协议或可靠性几乎没有讨论,这使人们对使用自动衡量标准,如嵌入式和N克计量标准提出质疑。 在此,我们提供了初步分析,以更好地理解这些衡量标准如何相互关联,并证明我们使用自动衡量标准的基础。 具体地说,我们调查了三个关于多样性和创造性一代的新标准的问题: (1) 嵌入式、N克制和LLM-as-a-Judge的衡量标准在多大程度上相互一致? (2) 每一类衡量标准有多可靠? (3) 在选择嵌入模型时,基于嵌入的衡量标准是否有力?

blocks.en: We use all generated responses from the main experiments. There are 3 generator models (Qwen3-1.7B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3), 4 datasets (Artificial Hivemind, Creativity Index, Novelty Bench, Creative Math), and 5 sampling methods (base, min- p p , verbalized, Multi-Turn, SEPO), all at temperature 0.7 0.7 . This gives 60 conditions, 58,090 58{,}090 responses, and 5,809 5{,}809 ten-response sets. LLM-as-a-judge is Gemini-3-Flash (judge temperature 1.0 1.0 ). It gives a 1–5 diversity score to each ten-response set and a 1–5 novelty score to each response. Novelty is judged relative to a reference set of ten base-sampling responses from the same model to the same prompt. We compute the automatic metrics on exactly the texts and reference sets the judge saw. Embedding-based metrics use BGE-M3 cosine distance. Diversity is the mean pairwise distance within a set; novelty is the distance to the nearest reference response. N-gram-based metrics use L-uniqueness, the fraction of a response’s tokens not covered by shared L L -grams, averaged over L = 5 , … , 12 L=5,\dots,12 . For diversity the other nine responses in the set serve as the reference (leave-one-out); for novelty the base references do. All correlations are Spearman’s ρ \rho . Confidence intervals are 95% percentile intervals from 1,000 1{,}000 bootstrap resamples of whole prompts.

blocks.en: Table 13 reports how closely the three metric families agree. At the level of method comparison, agreement is strong. For novelty, the judge and embedding metrics are nearly interchangeable (condition-wise ρ = 0.91 \rho=0.91 , ranking τ = 0.83 \tau=0.83 ), and both pairs involving the n-gram metric still reach ρ ≥ 0.72 \rho\geq 0.72 . Diversity shows moderate agreement across all pairs ( ρ = 0.55 \rho=0.55 – 0.67 0.67 , τ = 0.60 \tau=0.60 – 0.65 0.65 ). Conclusions about which methods produce more novel or diverse outputs therefore hold regardless of which metric family is used.
blocks.zh: 表13报告了三个衡量标准家庭的一致程度。 在方法比较方面,意见一致。 对于新颖性来说,判断和嵌入度量衡几乎可以互换(有条件的 ^ 0.91\rho = 0.91,排名为 ^ 0.83\tau = 0.83),涉及n克度量的两对相机仍然能达到 ^ 0.72\rho\geq 0.72 (英语). 多样性表明所有对齐都具有中度一致( ^ 0.55\rho= 0.55 — 0.67 0.67, ^ 0.60\tau= 0.60 — 0.65 0.65 ) 。 因此,无论使用哪一个指标家族,关于哪些方法能产生更新颖或更多样化的产出的结论都存在。

blocks.en: Agreement is weaker for individual outputs, and the two constructs behave differently. For novelty, response-wise correlations are high ( ρ = 0.66 \rho=0.66 – 0.80 0.80 ) but fall sharply once prompt effects are removed (prompt-wise ρ = 0.32 \rho=0.32 – 0.38 0.38 ). The metrics agree largely on which prompts elicit novel responses, but much less on which of the ten responses to the same prompt is most novel. For diversity, prompt-wise correlations ( ρ = 0.43 \rho=0.43 – 0.61 0.61 ) stay close to the response-wise values ( ρ = 0.39 \rho=0.39 – 0.65 0.65 ). Differences between methods’ response sets for the same prompt are therefore captured about as consistently as differences across prompts. Across both constructs, the judge–n-gram pair agrees least, which fits the gap between surface-level lexical overlap and the semantic judgments made by the LLM judge. Overall, the metric families support the same method-level conclusions but should not be treated as interchangeable for fine-grained, within-prompt assessments, especially for novelty. We therefore report all three families throughout.

blocks.en: We next ask whether the disagreement in Table 13 comes from measurement noise. Table 14 reports split-half reliability over prompts. Method rankings within each model × \times dataset pair are also stable across halves ( τ ¯ = 0.87 \bar{\tau}=0.87 – 0.97 0.97 , P5 ≥ 0.83 \geq 0.83 ). Novelty rankings are the most stable under the judge and embedding metrics ( τ ¯ ≥ 0.96 \bar{\tau}\geq 0.96 ). The n-gram metric is somewhat less stable for novelty ( τ ¯ = 0.87 \bar{\tau}=0.87 ), and the three metrics are comparable for diversity ( τ ¯ = 0.89 \bar{\tau}=0.89 – 0.92 0.92 ).

This supports reporting the three metric families together rather than treating any one as a noisy proxy for the others.

Condition-wise correlations are 0.97 0.97 – 0.99 0.99 for novelty and 0.87 0.87 – 0.98 0.98 for diversity, and response- and prompt-wise correlations are 0.85 0.85 – 0.94 0.94 . BGE-M3 and MPNet are nearly interchangeable ( ρ ≥ 0.94 \rho\geq 0.94 ). Qwen3 deviates slightly more, mainly for diversity.

blocks.en: Box 3: System Prompt Optimization Meta-Prompt # Objective You’re tasked to revise the current proposed system instruction for a downstream generation model. You will see the task, the current instruction archive, the history of proposed instruction candidates with marginal diversity scores, and the current proposed instruction with its evaluation result. Specifically, your goal is to revise the current generation instruction so that it elicits responses that are both: 1. high quality for the downstream task 2. diverse relative to responses elicited by the existing instruction archive. Important form constraint: the improved instruction is a reusable system instruction that will be applied to one user prompt at a time. It is not a replacement user prompt, not a prompt template, and not a request to generate many alternatives. It should steer how the model answers the user’s actual prompt once. The evaluator assigns each instruction a marginal diversity score: how much the instruction increases response diversity relative to the current instruction archive. Marginal diversity means the revised instruction should elicit responses that explore meaningfully different reasoning paths, content choices, perspectives, or solution strategies, not merely different wording, punctuation, formatting, tone, or visible output form. Keep the current instruction archive in mind as the reference set: a strong revision should be complementary to the archive and should avoid eliciting responses that follow the same strategy patterns already covered there. # Downstream Task Description {dataset task description} This search is shared across the following prompt set. Produce instruction branches that are broadly useful for this task type, not overfit to only one prompt. Each branch must preserve the individual user prompt at generation time while encouraging a distinct response mode, perspective, inference, abstraction, or reasoning direction. Use these prompts as references for task coverage, not content to copy; do not treat repeated topics, genres, or examples as the global task. Prompt set: {five training prompts, numbered [1]-[5]} # Current Instruction Archive <Current_Selected_Instruction_Archive> Empty </Current_Selected_Instruction_Archive> # Instruction Proposing History Base behavior is always an implicit reference. Avoid cross-round score comparisons. The history contains existing proposed instruction candidates, their marginal diversity scores, and any available feedback. Use this history as accumulated proposing experience for revising the current proposed instruction. Infer which candidate-level choices are associated with higher marginal diversity scores and which choices are associated with lower marginal diversity scores. Use marginal scores only as evidence of behavioral distance from the applicable archive. A higher marginal score is not evidence of better downstream quality and is not a reason to intensify complexity. Scores are noisy: if a high-scoring candidate is a replacement prompt, contains fill-in blanks, asks for a series of responses, lists the user’s constraints, exposes a planning step, changes the requested output form, mentions the archive/history/prompt set, or targets one concrete prompt, treat that shape as a failure even if its score is high. Use those lessons to decide what to preserve, remove, refine, or replace so the revision contributes a complementary semantic behavior while keeping the downstream task intact. The new instruction must be meaningfully different from every instruction in the current archive and history. <Recent_Completed_Round_History>Empty</Recent_Completed_Round_History> # Current Proposed Instruction with the corresponding score feedback <Current_Proposed_Candidate> <Instruction>Base behavior (no added system instruction)</Instruction> <Marginal_Diversity_Score higher_is_better="true" relative_to="current_selected_archive" aggregation="minimum_pair_distance">unscored</Marginal_Diversity_Score> </Current_Proposed_Candidate> # Requirements: - Treat downstream quality requirements as binding; improve marginal diversity among instructions likely to satisfy them across task subtypes. - Make the revised instruction complementary to the current archive. - Change how the model selects or develops the requested content, not its surface phrasing or visible output form. - Keep preparatory planning internal. - Prefer content generation over constraint management. - Adapt mechanisms to each request. - The response must contain only the requested answer and preserve every explicit content and output constraint. - Use the history to identify what has worked or failed before, then apply those lessons directly to the current proposed instruction. - The improved instruction must be a system instruction for answering the user’s actual prompt once. - The improved instruction must be complete natural-language prose, ready to use as-is; blocks.en: # Objective
blocks.zh: {\fn方正粗倩简体\fs12\an8\1cHFFFF00\b0} 目标

blocks.en: You’re tasked to revise the current proposed system instruction for a downstream generation model.
blocks.zh: 你的任务是修改目前提议的下游一代模式的系统指令。

blocks.en: You will see the task, the current instruction archive, the history of proposed instruction candidates with marginal diversity scores, and the current proposed instruction with its evaluation result.
blocks.zh: 您将看到任务、 当前的教学档案、 拟选的教学对象的历史, 以及当前拟选的教学及其评价结果。

blocks.en: Specifically, your goal is to revise the current generation instruction so that it elicits responses that are both:
blocks.zh: 具体地说,你的目标是修改目前的生成指令,从而引起以下两方面的反应:

blocks.en: 1. high quality for the downstream task
blocks.zh: 1.下游任务质量高.

blocks.en: 2. diverse relative to responses elicited by the existing instruction archive.
blocks.zh: 2. 与现有指令档案所引发的反应不同。

blocks.en: Important form constraint: the improved instruction is a reusable system instruction that will be applied to one user prompt at a time. It is not a replacement user prompt, not a prompt template, and not a request to generate many alternatives. It should steer how the model answers the user’s actual prompt once.
blocks.zh: 重要的形式约束:被改进的指令是一种可重复使用的系统指令,将一次被应用到一个用户的提示上. 这不是一个替换用户的提示,也不是一个即时模板,也不是一个生成许多替代品的请求. 它应该指导模型如何一次回答用户的实际提示。

blocks.en: The evaluator assigns each instruction a marginal diversity score: how much the instruction increases response diversity relative to the current instruction archive.
blocks.zh: 评价者为每个指令分配了边际多样性分数:相对于当前指令档案,该指令在多大程度上增加了响应多样性.

blocks.en: Marginal diversity means the revised instruction should elicit responses that explore meaningfully different reasoning paths, content choices, perspectives, or solution strategies, not merely different wording, punctuation, formatting, tone, or visible output form.
blocks.zh: 边际多样性是指订正指示应引起反应,探讨有意义的不同推理路径、内容选择、观点或解决方案战略,而不仅仅是不同的措辞、标出、格式、语气或可见输出形式。

blocks.en: Keep the current instruction archive in mind as the reference set: a strong revision should be complementary to the archive and should avoid eliciting responses that follow the same strategy patterns already covered there.
blocks.zh: 将现行指示存档作为参考:强有力的修订应补充档案,并避免引起遵循已涵盖的相同战略模式的反应。

blocks.en:
We use a joint-set adaptation of GEPA ( Agrawal et al., 2026 ) , which revises a
candidate set of ten system prompts using the pairwise divergence matrix and
per-prompt quality feedback. GEPA uses the same proposer ( gpt-oss-20b )
and a budget of 640 proposer requests, matching SEPO’s configured budget. Its
search score is the minimum pairwise JS divergence minus a soft penalty, λ \lambda times the fraction of prompts that fail the quality gates. We run λ ∈ { 0 , 0.05 , 0.1 , 0.2 , 1 } \lambda\in\{0,0.05,0.1,0.2,1\} , where λ = 0 \lambda=0 uses quality only as
advisory feedback.

We do not impose a hard quality threshold during the GEPA iterations because it
leaves no qualified joint set to deploy. We ran this hard-constrained variant on
Artificial Hivemind with Qwen3-1.7B, using the same instruction- and
response-quality thresholds as SEPO. The search first maximized the number of
prompts passing both gates, and would maximize the minimum pairwise divergence
only once all ten passed. None of the 640 proposer requests produced a qualified
ten-prompt set: GEPA kept at most five of the ten prompts qualified at once. Of
the 599 requests that yielded a scorable set, only ten reached five passing
prompts, and 473 473 ( 79 % 79\% ) had two or fewer. In the best set, all ten prompts
passed the instruction gate, but five failed the response-quality gate. We
therefore use a soft penalty, under which every run returns a deployable set,
sweep over the penalty weight λ \lambda , and compare GEPA fairly with SEPO at
similar quality.

blocks.en: Appendix P Limitations of Automatic Creativity Metrics
blocks.zh: 附录P 自动创意计量的限制

blocks.en:
Our numerical diversity and novelty metrics are heuristic proxies for
creativity. Prior work documents inconsistencies across automatic creativity
measures and domains, and shows that N N -gram-based measures can primarily
capture lexical variation rather than conceptual creativity ( Lu et al., 2026 ) .
Embedding-based distances measure semantic separation, which need not imply
creative originality, while N N -gram-based scores can reward changes in wording
without corresponding changes in ideas. Text length may also influence these
measurements and should be examined as a potential confound. We adopt
established, widely used measurement approaches to facilitate comparison with
prior work, but improvements on these proxies do not by themselves establish
improvements in human-perceived creativity. Broader human studies across tasks
and participant populations are needed to assess whether the measured gains
correspond to creativity as perceived by humans. One direction is to collect
human preference judgments under explicit criteria and use them to train a
reward model, as has been done for image–text data
curation ( Zhang et al., 2023 ) ; whether this approach transfers to
creativity assessment remains open.

blocks.en: Appendix Q Case Study: What Changes Under System-Prompt Optimization?
blocks.zh: 附录 Q 研究:系统快速优化下有什么变化?.

blocks.en:
SEPO optimizes a pool of system instructions, rather than individual
answers. The supplied optimized instruction list includes explicit
operations such as stakeholder-based reframing and constraint-oriented
organization. For example, one instruction asks the model to
“choose an alternate stakeholder” and let that stakeholder’s concerns
shape the response. In contrast, one SEP instruction asks the model to
construct its answer around a unifying idea, emotion, or metaphor.
The distinction is therefore in the requested response behavior,
not merely in alternative wording.
blocks.zh:
SEPO优化了一套系统指令,而不是个人
答对. 所提供的优化指令清单包括:
以利益攸关方为基础的调整和以制约为导向的行动
组织。 例如,一项指令要求模型
" 选择另一个利益有关者 " ,让该利益有关者的关切
形成反应。 相比之下,SEP的一条指示要求模型
围绕一个统一的思想、情感或比喻构建答案。
因此,区别在于所要求的反应行为,
不仅仅是替代措辞。
